coverageNote: Read all 47 scoped Markdown files, grouped as five subdomain folders plus one domain-level/shared unit, through 3a implementer simulation, 3b Vision Rubric scoring, and 3c devil's-advocate probing.

findings.forcedInvention: When an unresolved product, authority, or contract decision is encountered, an implementer must invent whether it is currently blocking and when it must be escalated.
findings.failureScenario: Different teams treat the same unresolved decision as a blocker, a default, or deferred work, then reopen it after dependent contracts have shipped.

findings.claim: A room can be both granted and independently claimed, but precedence, refusal, and post-revocation survival are undefined.

evidence.excerpt: Two authority provenances can exist on one room and no source in this domain defines precedence, whether the second is refused, or whether the grant survives a successful claim.
Undefined: what a claim does when it lands on an already-granted room, what a grant does to an org that already holds a room claim, and which provenance survives if a grant is revoked.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose which organisation may write, sell, or retain room authority when grant and claim coexist.
findings.failureScenario: A room remains bookable under the wrong authority or an authorised operator loses access during a disputed revocation.

findings.claim: No component owns the transition from a claimed zero-room record to a room that can be booked and harvested.

evidence.excerpt: 16.05.02's claim flow ends before a room exists and 16.01.02 assumes rooms are created by someone already present. Neither owns the transition.

findings.forcedInvention: Create an owner, event, and authority handoff for post-claim room creation.
findings.failureScenario: Seeded records can be claimed but never become bookable rooms, leaving the cold-start registry unable to refresh itself.

findings.claim: Studio access and logistics are not owned by any 16.03 feature and cannot simply inherit the venue-only feature.

evidence.excerpt: A first-floor project studio with no lift and a Hammond to carry is a real booking-breaker, is not acoustics, and is not in any of 16.03's four features.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose the owning component and data/interaction model for studio load-in, access, and logistics facts.
findings.failureScenario: A studio booking is presented as viable even though the required equipment or performer cannot physically access the room.

findings.claim: The org-only gear publication path excludes home studios and sole-trader rehearsal rooms from backline discovery.

evidence.excerpt: A bedroom studio or a one-person rehearsal business has no org entity and its gear is a personal collection with no publication path.
It is an unresolved precondition of D-06, not a consequence of it, and it blocks real supply.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose a personal-collection publication source, a single-person organisation model, or an explicit supply exclusion.
findings.failureScenario: The most common smaller studios and rehearsal rooms disappear from gear filters despite possessing the requested equipment.

findings.claim: The dry-hire room plus freelance engineer compound has no owning feature or cross-domain responsibility boundary.

evidence.excerpt: Cross-domain compound (dry hire + a 05 freelance engineer) — who owns it? The platform's clearest structural cross-sell, currently nobody's feature.
It will fall down the gap between 16 and 05 unless assigned.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose the owning component and its booking, permission, pricing, and cancellation responsibility.
findings.failureScenario: A room and engineer cannot be reserved atomically, or the reservation has conflicting authority and settlement behaviour.

findings.claim: The reservation lifecycle assumes automatic refunds and contested-fund handling that pass-through payments cannot implement.

evidence.excerpt: D-04 (the ladder is enforced automatically) is unimplementable on pass-through; pass-through also cannot hold contested no-show funds or fund an insolvent Operator's cascade refunds.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose a payment model or weaken the specified cancellation, refund, and disputed-fund guarantees.
findings.failureScenario: The platform promises automatic remedies it cannot execute, leaving disputes and insolvency refunds unfunded.

findings.claim: Exporting a client's display name to a shared third-party calendar lacks a resolved lawful basis and controller/processor treatment.

evidence.excerpt: Needs an owner call on the principle and a lawful-basis determination (controller/processor split, GDPR Art. 6, and whether disclosure suffices or consent is required).

findings.forcedInvention: Choose the lawful basis, party roles, notice or consent requirement, and exported-name policy.
findings.failureScenario: A musician's identity is copied into a calendar shared with third parties without a justified disclosure model.

findings.claim: The venue backline model contradicts itself on whether backline is a 15.07 read-through or a locally typed boolean field.

evidence.excerpt: D-06 and G7 say backline is not typed here, but the Checkable tier lists backline present y/n among its six core fields.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose the source of truth, any permitted shadow value, and how validation resolves the two representations.
findings.failureScenario: Backline search and rider checks read different values for the same room and present a false availability result.

findings.claim: Conditional venue facts have three incompatible shapes without a canonical data contract or consumer interpretation.

evidence.excerpt: What remains is strictly the unification call — three shapes, one platform.
Whether these become one shared model or stay per-field is a structural decision above this file.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose a canonical conditional-value schema and the matching, filtering, and display rules that consume it.
findings.failureScenario: Capacity, curfew, hospitality, and accessibility consumers interpret conditions differently and make contradictory booking decisions.

findings.claim: The authority policy for owner-versus-first-hand reports is unmapped for the remaining field classes.

evidence.excerpt: The remaining classes are unmapped and no later stage maps them.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose which source prevails, or how a contest is resolved, for each unmapped field class.
findings.failureScenario: Equivalent disputes apply inconsistent authority rules, producing either false public facts or unjustified owner overrides.

findings.claim: The post-gig report anonymity floor is unresolved for low-traffic rooms where month-level timestamps do not de-identify a contributor.

evidence.excerpt: A room with one gig a month is not de-identified by either; accept the residual, suppress the harvest, or hold reports until a second independent party corroborates.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose the residual-identification policy and the suppression or corroboration threshold.
findings.failureScenario: A contributor can be inferred from a correction, exposing them to retaliation, or the system suppresses the only available safety-relevant report.

findings.claim: The authored US statutory profile lacks the required legal instruments and issuer mappings, and post-launch profile authorship governance is unassigned.

evidence.excerpt: What are the US instruments and issuers for the five slots? D-06's live PENDING; this unblocks the ingest mapping row for the statutory class.
Nothing says who owns it or what evidence a profile must cite before its slots go live.

findings.forcedInvention: Invent statutory slot vocabulary, issuers, evidence criteria, and the governing author for legal profiles.
findings.failureScenario: Statutory records are mapped to the wrong instrument or become silently authoritative without a governed legal source.

findings.claim: The rider-to-room result is named conflict by 16 and shortfall by 18, with no unified outcome vocabulary or qualifier contract.

evidence.excerpt: The two sides name the same outcome differently — 16 says conflict, 18 says shortfall — and one contract must carry one vocabulary.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose the shared result enum, mapping, and qualifier semantics at the 16-to-18 boundary.
findings.failureScenario: An advance workflow handles the same failed comparison differently from the matcher, yielding inconsistent show-readiness actions.

findings.claim: The proposal to treat a lockout billing cycle as a completion-equivalent has no ratified cross-component event contract.

evidence.excerpt: It is a proposal from this feature into another's lifecycle and needs that feature's agreement, not this one's assertion — a cross-component event contract.
What is still open is ratification of a cross-component event contract.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose the event owner, acceptance rules, and completion semantics for a recurring lockout billing cycle.
findings.failureScenario: Lockout supply either never generates freshness evidence or emits duplicate or untrusted harvest events.

findings.claim: Pooled gear has neither a calendar owner nor a defined booking-time conflict and dependency-capture rule.

evidence.excerpt: 16.06.05 carries atomicity, the resource graph and failure naming, but no pooled-asset surfacing rule and no book-time dependency capture.
The pooled mic has no calendar owner today — the gap that produces the double-sale.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose the allocatable resource owner and the second-booking enforcement and notification behaviour.
findings.failureScenario: The same pooled mic or backline asset is promised to simultaneous reservations.

findings.claim: A statutory operating-condition change has no resolved cascade behaviour for already confirmed bookings.

evidence.excerpt: Does a statutory condition change cascade to confirmed bookings automatically, or is it Operator-initiated?

findings.forcedInvention: Choose the cascade owner and notification, cancellation, and remediation behaviour when a statutory condition changes.
findings.failureScenario: Confirmed shows remain advanced against an invalid curfew or the platform performs an irreversible mass update without authority.
